6º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 2

Past simple: regular and irregular verbs

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about finished actions in the past (acciones terminadas)
  • Add -ed to regular verbs with the right spelling
  • Learn the most common irregular verbs
  • Make negatives and questions with did / didn't

Para pensar

En español decimos «ayer jugué» y «ayer fui». En inglés, «jugué» es played, pero «fui» no es «goed». ¿Por qué?

Explicación

What is the past simple?

We use the past simple for actions that started and finished in the past: «I visited my cousins last summer», «We watched a film yesterday». We often say when it happened.

En castellano: equivale a nuestro pretérito: «visité», «vimos». Una gran ventaja del inglés: el verbo no cambia según la persona. «I played», «you played», «he played», «they played». ¡No hay que memorizar seis terminaciones como en español!

Regular verbs: -ed

Regular verbs add -ed: walk → walked, play → played, watch → watched, help → helped.

Spelling rules: verbs ending in -e add only -d: like → liked, dance → danced. Consonant + y changes to -ied: study → studied, cry → cried (but play → played, because a vowel comes before the y). Short verbs ending in consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter: stop → stopped, plan → planned.

How do you say -ed?

The ending -ed has three sounds. After most sounds it is /d/: played, cleaned, opened. After sounds like p, k, s, sh, ch it is /t/: walked («wokt»), watched («wocht»), helped («helpt»).

After t or d it is a new syllable /ɪd/: wanted («uóntid»), needed («nídid»), visited. En castellano: casi nunca se pronuncia «-ed» completo; solo cuando el verbo acaba en t o d. Di en voz alta: «I walked to the park and I wanted an ice cream».

Irregular verbs

Many common verbs are irregular: they don't add -ed. You need to learn them by heart (de memoria). Here are some of the most useful: go → went, have → had, eat → ate, see → saw, buy → bought, get → got, make → made, come → came, take → took, write → wrote, swim → swam, run → ran.

The verb to be has two forms: was (I, he, she, it) and were (you, we, they). «It was sunny», «We were at the beach».

Tricks to learn irregular verbs

Group them by sound and it's easier (agrúpalos por cómo suenan). -ought / -aught: buy → bought, bring → brought, think → thought, teach → taught. i → a: swim → swam, sing → sang, drink → drank, begin → began. Same form: put → put, cut → cut, hit → hit.

Make flashcards (tarjetas): the verb on one side, the past on the other. Practise five verbs a day. Sing them with a rhythm: «go, went – see, saw – eat, ate!». En castellano: no intentes aprender cien de golpe; los veinte más usados ya cubren casi todo.

Negatives with didn't

To make a negative we use didn't (did not) + the verb in its normal form: «I didn't play football yesterday», «She didn't go to school». Careful: after didn't we never use the past: not «didn't went».

The verb to be is different: it doesn't need didn't. We say «I wasn't tired», «They weren't at home». En castellano: did ya lleva el pasado; por eso el verbo vuelve a su forma básica, igual que en el presente con doesn't.

Questions with did

For questions we put Did at the beginning and the verb in its normal form: «Did you enjoy the trip?» – «Yes, I did. / No, I didn't». «Did he see the dolphins?» – «Yes, he did».

With question words: «Where did you go?», «What did you eat?», «When did they arrive?». With to be: «Was it fun?», «Were you scared?». Time words for the past: yesterday, last night, last week, last summer, two days ago, in 2024.

Reading: my best holiday

Read Hugo's text: «Last summer I went to Asturias with my family. We stayed in a small house near the sea. On the first day it rained, so we visited a museum. Then the sun came out and we swam every day. I tried cheese from the mountains – it was delicious! We didn't take many photos, but I wrote a diary. It was the best holiday ever.»

Find six regular verbs and six irregular ones. Which verbs are in the negative?

Let's practise: guess my weekend

Play in groups. Write three sentences about last weekend: two true and one false (una falsa). «I went to the cinema. I ate sushi. I played tennis». Your classmates ask questions to find the false one: «Did you go with your family?», «What film did you see?».

Then write a short text about a special day. Use time order words: first, then, after that, finally. Consejo: repasa al final si cada verbo está en pasado y si después de did has usado la forma normal.

Past simple

Ejercicios

  1. Write the past: play, like, cry, plan.

  2. Write the past: go, eat, see, buy.

  3. Complete with was or were: «The film ___ great. We ___ happy.»

  4. Make it negative: «He wrote a letter.»

  5. Make a question: «You had lunch at school.»

  6. How do you pronounce -ed in «wanted», «watched», «played»?

  7. Correct: «Yesterday I swimmed in the pool.»

  8. Answer: «Did you watch TV last night?» (no)

  9. Translate: «La semana pasada visitamos a mi abuela.»

  10. Write three sentences about your last birthday.

Practica

  1. The past of «walk» is…

    1. A) walkt
    2. B) walked
    3. C) walk

  2. The past of «go» is…

    1. A) goed
    2. B) gone
    3. C) went

  3. The past of «study» is…

    1. A) studied
    2. B) studyed
    3. C) studed

  4. «___ you enjoy the party?»

    1. A) Do
    2. B) Were
    3. C) Did

  5. «She didn't ___ the bus.»

    1. A) took
    2. B) take
    3. C) takes

  6. «They ___ at the beach yesterday.»

    1. A) were
    2. B) was
    3. C) did

  7. The past of «eat» is…

    1. A) eated
    2. B) ate
    3. C) eaten

  8. Which is a past time expression?

    1. A) every day
    2. B) now
    3. C) two days ago

  9. The past of «stop» is…

    1. A) stopped
    2. B) stoped
    3. C) stopt

  10. In «wanted», -ed sounds…

    1. A) /t/
    2. B) /ɪd/
    3. C) /d/

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el pasado simple; Cómo se forma el pasado de los verbos regulares y su ortografía; Qué son los verbos irregulares y algunos ejemplos; Cómo se hacen negativas y preguntas con did.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

Past simpleAcciones terminadas en el pasado.
-edPasado regular: walked, played.
-ied / doble consonantestudied · stopped.
go → wentIrregular muy frecuente.
was / werePasado de to be.
didn't + verboNegativa: I didn't go.
Did…?Pregunta: Did you see it?
agoHace: two days ago = hace dos días.

Soluciones

  1. B) Regular: + -ed.
  2. C) Irregular.
  3. A) Consonante + y → -ied.
  4. C) Pregunta en pasado: Did.
  5. B) Tras didn't, forma normal.
  6. A) They + were.
  7. B) Irregular.
  8. C) Ago = hace.
  9. A) Se dobla la p.
  10. B) Tras t o d, sílaba nueva.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. played, liked, cried, planned.
  2. went, ate, saw, bought.
  3. was, were.
  4. He didn't write a letter.
  5. Did you have lunch at school?
  6. /ɪd/, /t/, /d/.
  7. Yesterday I swam in the pool.
  8. No, I didn't.
  9. Last week we visited my grandma.
  10. Model answer: I had a party. My friends came to my house. We ate a chocolate cake.
